name: Software, tech & AI
description: Everyday truths about writing code, shipping software, and machine learning.
sentences: Clean code reads like well written prose, clear enough that comments feel almost unneeded.
A good API is easy to use correctly and genuinely hard to use by mistake.
Version control lets a whole team edit one project without stepping on each other.
Caching is one of the two hard problems in computing, along with naming things.
Every bug caught in testing is a support ticket that never has to be written.
A large language model predicts the next token based on the patterns it has seen.
Machine learning finds structure in data that no one took the time to spell out.
Shipping a small change today often beats waiting months for the perfect release.
The cloud is really just someone else's computer that you rent by the hour.
Good documentation is a gift you leave for the exhausted version of your future self.
Premature optimization wastes effort on problems the program may never actually have.
A neural network learns by adjusting millions of weights one small step at a time.
Automated tests give you the courage to change code without holding your breath.
Latency is the delay a user feels, and users notice every wasted millisecond.
Open source software runs quietly beneath almost every app on your phone.
A model is only ever as good as the data it was trained on, flaws and all.
Refactoring improves the shape of the code without changing what it actually does.
The hardest part of programming is often understanding the problem, not the syntax.
Encryption turns readable messages into noise that only the right key can undo.
Progress in AI tends to arrive in sudden, uneven leaps rather than a smooth line.
